::: {.column-screen-inset}

```{ojs plot-opts}
//| output: false

// shared options for all plots
stats_opts = ({
         style: { fontFamily: "var(--sans-serif)", fontSize: 12, overflow: "visible" },
         width: 0.45 * width,
    marginLeft: 130,
  marginBottom: 40,
     insetLeft: 10,
             y: { grid: true, label: null, tickSize: 0, tickPadding: 2, domain: task_order },
             x: { line: true },
             r: { label: "N", range: [1, 4] },
         color: { scheme: "Turbo", domain: task_order, reverse: true }
})

tip_vars = ({ "Dataset": "dataset" })

// slider for the minimum value of a sample size variable
min_n_input = (label) => {
  const form = Inputs.range([0, 300], { label: label, step: 1, value: 30 })
  // set how far to fill the slider track (see _style)
  const range = form.querySelector("input[type=range]")
  const fill = () => range.style.setProperty("--fill", (range.valueAsNumber - range.min) / (range.max - range.min))
  form.addEventListener("input", fill)
  fill()
  return form
}
```

::: {.plot-inputs}

```{ojs input-min-n-scores}
viewof min_n_scores = url_bound("min_n", min_n_input("Min N scores"))
```

:::

```{ojs filter-n-scores}
//| output: false
stats_n_scores = stats_coded.filter(d => d.n_scores >= min_n_scores)

// order of tasks for every plot's y axis and colors -- by highest reliability,
// with tasks that have none last
task_order = d3.groupSort(stats_coded,
  g => -(d3.max(g, d => d.empirical_rxx) ?? -Infinity),
  d => d.Task)
```

::: {layout="[ [1,1] ]"}

```{ojs plot-reliability}
// reliability
Plot.plot({
  ...stats_opts,
  x: { label: "Empirical reliability", line: true, domain: [0, 1] },
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(stats_n_scores, {
      x: "empirical_rxx",
      y: "Task",
      stroke: "Task",
      r: "n_scores",
      tip: true,
      channels: tip_vars
    })
]
})
```


```{ojs redivis}
redivis = import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/redivis@0.4.2/+esm")

// get stats table from workflow
async function getStats() {
  console.log('getting stats')
  // sign in with workflow read access up front -- the browser client otherwise
  // signs in with only data access, and then makes the user sign in again when
  // the workflow table request is rejected for its scope
  await redivis.authorize({ scope: 'workflow.read' })
  const rows = await redivis
    .user('mikabr')
    .workflow('levante_data_latest_psychometrics:xhxj')
    .table('task_x_dataset_combined:h9gb')
    .toRowsArray()
  console.log('got stats')
  return rows;
}

stats = await getStats()
```
